workspaces.heading: Where your workspaces are.
workspaces.text: Your top workspace is in your **Documents** folder, on this laptop.

whyT3Code: T3 Code names your threads for you, saves a version of your work in one click, and keeps gaining features. It lists your workspaces, so you can start each conversation in the one the work belongs to.
privacy: What Anthropic does with your conversations depends on your Claude plan.

**On Claude Free, Pro or Max**, Anthropic's consumer terms apply, and its **Help improve Claude** setting decides whether Anthropic may use your chats and coding sessions to improve Claude. With it on, Anthropic may keep that data for up to 5 years; with it off, it keeps to its 30-day data retention period. To check it or turn it off, open claude.ai's [data privacy controls](https://claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls).

**On Claude Team or Enterprise**, under contract with Anthropic, your conversations aren't used for training, nor is anything the agent reads for you. In Anthropic's words: "By default, we will not use your inputs or outputs from our commercial products (e.g. Claude for Work, Anthropic API, Claude Gov, etc.) to train our models."

**On Team or Enterprise, they're deleted within 30 days.** Anthropic deletes them from its back-end storage systems within 30 days, unless its automated trust and safety systems flag one as breaking its [Usage Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup). A flagged conversation is kept for up to 2 years.
**Feedback is the exception.** If you send Anthropic feedback, such as with a thumbs up or down on claude.ai, it keeps that whole conversation for up to 5 years and may use it to train its models.

Anthropic's own pages say more: [Is my data used for model training?](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996868-is-my-data-used-for-model-training), [How long do you store my organization's data?](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996866-how-long-do-you-store-my-organization-s-data) and [Updates to our consumer terms](https://www.anthropic.com/news/updates-to-our-consumer-terms).

connectors.name: Gmail
connectors.what: search and read your email, and write drafts for you to check and send

connectors.name: Google Calendar
connectors.what: see your calendar and, when you ask, add or change events

connectors.name: Asana
connectors.what: see your tasks and projects and, when you ask, create or update tasks
connectors.note: For Asana: at the top of Asana's page, choose your team's workspace. Unless your team works there, don't choose the one named after your work email's domain (the part after the @). Asana makes that one for everyone with an email address there.

extraTools.question: Would you like the agent to be able to publish and manage Apps Script projects for you?
extraTools.signIn: A browser window will open. Choose the Google account you use for Apps Script and allow what clasp asks for. Come back here when the page says "Logged in!".
extraTools.settings: On the Apps Script settings page, check the account shown at the top right is the one you just signed in with. Then click Google Apps Script API and switch it on. Only you can change this setting.
